Mesh

class ibfs.mesh.Mesh(x0: float, x1: float, nx: int, y0: float, y1: float, ny: int)[source]

Bases: object

Holds information on a two-dimensional uniform mesh with \(\Delta = \Delta x = \Delta y\) over the spatial domain

\[\Omega = \left[ x_0, x_1 \right] \times \left[ y_0, y_1 \right].\]

The attributes self.x and self.y contain the coordinates of the grid at cell centers. The grid is staggered, so \(x\)-velocities are stored at right/left cell faces, \(y\)-velocities at top/bottom cell faces, and the pressure is stored at cell centers. This class also holds two-dimensional arrays to store the \(x\) velocity field, \(y\) velocity field and the pressure.

Parameters:

  • x0 (float) – \(x\) location of the left boundary (inflow)

  • x1 (float) – \(x\) location of the right boundary (outflow)

  • nx (int) – number of cells in the x direction

  • y0 (float) – \(y\) location of the bottom boundary

  • y1 (float) – \(y\) location of the top boundary

  • ny (int) – number of cells in the y direction

generate_meshgrids(output_torch: bool | None = False) → List[array] | List[tensor][source]

Generate meshgrids for the \(u\), \(v\), and \(p\) fields as a list [Xu, Yu, Xv, Yv, Xp, Yp].

Parameters:

output_torch (Optional[bool], defaults to False) – outputs the meshgrids as torch tensors if True, and as numpy/cupy arrays otherwise. (Torch is often used in tests/ for its autodiff capabilities.)

Return type:

List[xp.array] | List[torch.tensor]

info()[source]

Print basic information about the mesh.
